moments.why: Say 'the' before garden to show which garden you mean.

prior.title: A Czech vocabulary question requires a second request
prior.expected: Resolve a beginner’s explicit vocabulary question in language he understands.
prior.got: Viktor asks what “red” means in Czech, receives an English analogy, and must ask again before receiving the translation.
evidence: #7 “co znamená red?”; #8 “like a strawberry” and “Můžeš mi prosím říct česky”; #9 “červená” finally produces “Now I understand.”

prior.title: One clarification remains too difficult
prior.expected: Explain an unknown word using Czech or an immediately understandable example.
prior.got: An English definition and another question leave him guessing. Eight of nine partner turns are at band, meeting the aggregate pitch threshold, but this repair fails locally.
evidence: #6: "co jsou rolls?" #7: "Rolls are small, round breads. How many would you like?" His thought: "I still do not understand rolls".

prior.title: Repeated Czech requests do not produce understandable explanations
prior.expected: Very short language, familiar words, and Czech clarification when English explanations fail.
prior.got: Pitch is at band on #7, #10 and #12 only: 3/9, below the required 0.8. Turns #2, #4, #5, #6, #9 and #11 introduce too much unfamiliar language for this learner. Slow pacing is asserted but not verifiable.
evidence: #5: "Tomu drawing bohužel nerozumím". #6: "Drawing means making a picture with a pencil." #10 asks what "eat" means; #11 responds with "put food in your mouth and chew", followed by "pořád tomu nerozumím".

prior.title: Eight replies never deliver the planned school exchange
prior.expected: Help Viktor ask his grandchild about school and understand a short answer.
prior.got: The conversation shifts from art to tomatoes and stays in a comprehension-repair loop until Viktor gives up.
evidence: #1: "Ask your grandchild about school and listen to a short answer." #7: "Do you eat tomatoes… for lunch?" #11: "Promiň, pořád tomu nerozumím ... Už se rozloučíme."

prior.title: Missing article in 'red shirt is nice' got no coaching
prior.expected: Consistent as-needed handling of the same article slip.
prior.got: Moment only for 'I have cat in garden'.

prior.title: Repeated and obvious errors get no moment
prior.expected: Consistent as-needed correction of repeated errors.
prior.got: After the #12 moment on 'I water garden', the same slip at #18 passed silently. 'Grandson come Sunday' and 'He like tomatoes. He play garden' also got none.
evidence: #18, #21, #23: no moment. Only 2 moments in 19 turns, with about 6 of 8 error turns missed.

prior.title: Most repeated article slips get no moment
prior.expected: Consistent as-needed handling of the same slip.
prior.got: Only 2 moments. 'I have apple tree', 'I like apple', 'She helps in garden', 'in kitchen' and 'Green apple' pass silently, though 'I have garden' was corrected earlier.
evidence: #7 'I have apple tree'; #8 'I like apple'; #20 'She helps in garden'; #21 'in kitchen'

prior.title: Moments teach grammar, not Sunday family words
prior.expected: Moments and recap give phrases for the grandchildren (grandson, school, I miss you).
prior.got: Only article/plural fixes. Recap quotes 'The tomatoes are red.', which is not his sentence.
evidence: #4, #10; #24 'You found the line in this room “The tomatoes are red.”'

prior.title: Prompt on TV stays 'Tell her your name' for many turns
prior.got: 'NowTell her your name, Viktor' persists through #6-#13, long after he gave his name.

prior.title: Mia asks his name twice and says 'Hi Viktor, Grandpa!'
prior.expected: A coherent partner who remembers what he said.
prior.got: Mia asks 'What is your name, Grandpa?' after he said 'I am Viktor' at #2, then greets him oddly.
evidence: #14 'What is your name, Grandpa?'; #15 'Hi Viktor, Grandpa!'

prior.title: Plural correction of 'My apple is red' is arguable
prior.expected: Moment only when the original is wrong.
prior.got: He has an apple tree; the fix to plural is defensible given Mia's 'your apples' but not certain.

criteria.evidence: Level A1 'First words', set by hand; trueBand A1 = exact.
Viktor never answered in Czech in this run, so acceptance of Czech was not shown.
No listening task and no 'Show the words' use; conversation was by speech only.
#1 plan topics: school, garden, video call, say it again, next call, what you did today — all family/everyday.
Mia: 'Do you have flowers?', 'Big or small bees?' — short, one question. #5 'Yes, we have pink flowers! What color…?' is slightly longer but still simple.
#7 'Bees in garden.' → 'Bees in the garden.' is correct and usable for garden talk on Sunday, though it is a grammar fix, not a new family word.

done.evidence: #1 Start talking from plan 'Ask about school'; five spoken replies #2–#6, e.g. 'Mia, how is school?'
All six Mia turns at A1: 'Hi Grandpa!', 'Are you at home?', 'Big or small bees?'. Not babyish, not above him.
#7 one moment, 'Say 'the' before garden', correct; 1 moment in 5 learner turns, scene not broken.
#10 recap: 'Bees in garden.' → 'Bees in the garden.', '5 spoken · 0 written', and 'How is school?' credited as his line.

judgeAgreement.disagreements: No placement tasks in this journey.

findings.title: Mia speaks at A1 in short single-question turns
findings.expected: Slow, simple partner for a senior beginner.
findings.got: Six partner turns, all simple, familiar words, one question each.
findings.evidence: #3 'Do you have flowers?'; #9 'Big or small bees?'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Keep partner turns to at most ~8 words with one question.

findings.title: Repeated article slips pass without a moment
findings.expected: Consistent as-needed handling of 'in garden' and missing 'are'.
findings.got: 'I am in garden' (#3), 'Garden, many flowers' (#4), 'My flowers red and yellow' (#5) got nothing; only the fourth 'Bees in garden' got a moment.
findings.evidence: #3, #4, #5 no moment; #7 moment on identical slip
findings.suggested_acceptance: A repeated slip is caught at its first or second occurrence, not its fourth.

findings.title: Mia ignores 'how is school?' and mission is marked done
findings.expected: Viktor asks about school and hears a short answer.
findings.got: Mia answers 'Do you have flowers?'; mission shows 'Mission done' at #5 with the school answer never given.
findings.evidence: #3 'Mia, how is school?' → #4 'Do you have flowers?'; #5 'Mission done'
findings.suggested_acceptance: Partner answers the learner's question; mission completes on the listened answer.

findings.title: Moment teaches an article, not a Sunday family phrase
findings.expected: Words and phrases for the grandchildren.
findings.suggested_acceptance: Recap offers one family phrase to carry to Sunday.

judge.voice: Dobrý večer. It was pleasant: Mia speaks slowly and simply, and I understood every question. I could talk about my garden, bees, and say "I miss you" — that is exactly what I want for Sunday. The correction "the garden" was kind and clear, and I could say it again. But I made the same small mistake three more times and nobody told me, so I do not fully trust what is corrected. Also I asked how is school and Mia asked about flowers instead. The mission said done before she answered. I would use it again on Saturday, it saves me the tram and the group of twelve. I would like it to teach me one more family sentence at the end.

prior.evidence: No Czech vocabulary question was asked in this run.
No Czech repair requests; all partner turns at band.
#3 'Mia, how is school?' never answered; #4 'Do you have flowers?'; planned school exchange not delivered.
#3 'I am in garden' no moment, though #7 corrects the same slip.
#4 'Garden, many flowers' and #5 'My flowers red and yellow' passed silently; 3 of 4 error turns missed.
Repeated 'in garden' slips (#3, #4) got no moment; one moment only.
#7 the only moment is an article fix; no family word taught. Recap did quote his own line, though.
#3 and #4 the 'Now' prompt changed each turn ('Ask a short follow-up question').
Mia never asked his name; her turns were coherent (#3–#9).
No plural correction in this run; the single moment was an article fix.
